pr_body:
Classname (the plugin entry point) is not needed for Stable plugins, but current code for transport protocol deserialization/serialization requires a classname to be present.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/98584
pr_title: Making classname optional in Transport protocol

review_comment: This roundtripping occurs in a couple other places in this test. Perhaps move it to a helper method like `PluginDescriptor roundTripDescriptor(PluginDescriptor info)`?

Question: do we have a policy of not throwing in constructors? (I guess not, since these read methods can throw) Or a preference to not do so?
Otherwise, I'd like to add some sanity checks (e.g. isStable <-> classname == null && moduleName == null), throwing IllegalArgumentException if not met.
Throwing in constructors is fine, if the arguments are not valid

I will add some checks in the constructors then. 
I also noticed that `toXContent` and `toString` are "outdated": they do not include all fields. I would update them, but I am wondering about `toXContent`. Is it used? A quick look seems to indicate it is used by `PluginsAndModules` and `PluginsAndModules` (for stats and report via NodeInfo).
I'd think it is safe to add the missing fields and omit classname/moduleName if null (if it is not already done by `XContentBuilder`!) 
What do you think?
I would use a separate PR to add the missing fields - also maybe check the git history & previous PRs to see if they were deliberately omitted or not
Sounds like a good plan, will do!
